_doc: Parks outside the bucket list, transcribed 2026-11-06. Entries with an operator URL are official (confidence confirmed). Entries marked confidence likely/unverified rest on local press or directory listings because the city site blocks automated access (Sisters, Culver, Redmond).

parks.name: Crooked River Park
parks.note: Two children's play areas, river access to the Crooked River, and a fenced dog park.

parks.name: Gervais Park
parks.address: 175 NW Meadow Lakes Dr, Prineville, OR 97754
parks.note: Nature park next to the Crook County Library, with a play structure and a short trail.

parks.name: Harwood Park
parks.note: Shady creekside park; playground installed in 2019.

parks.name: Ochoco Creek Park
parks.note: Home of Castle Park, Prineville's most popular park.

parks.name: Pioneer Park
parks.note: Downtown by the courthouse, with a toddler playground and a log cabin museum.

parks.name: Stryker Park
parks.note: Kiwanis Splash Park, a playground for ages 2-5, and an inclusive play area added in 2024.

parks.name: Yellowpine Park
parks.note: Quiet neighborhood park with a large playground.

parks.name: Finley Butte Park
parks.note: Sports complex with playgrounds, ball fields and pickleball courts.

parks.name: Frontier Heritage Park
parks.note: Next to the La Pine Community Center.

parks.name: Village Green Park
parks.note: Downtown Sisters park between Elm and Fir streets, with a gazebo, barbecue area and restrooms. The city won a 2019 state grant to replace the play structure.

parks.name: Culver City Park
parks.note: Directory listings mention a splash pad, slides and swings; a skatepark and pickleball courts opened in October 2025. Playground not confirmed by an official source.
